notes.text: Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen. That line has had 52% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:45 together.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 64% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 185:30 together.
Matt Tomkins was added to the roster on Oct 24.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 50% of the team’s power-play time in 15 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, down from 30% last season.
Connor Hellebuyck joined from WPG on Oct 24.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Devils (9-5-0) beat Vegas 5-2 on Friday, and the Oilers have won three straight. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (second in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for ninth).

The Oilers’ record (.800) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.627), largely thanks to their finishing. The Devils have played better than their record (.643) says: their chances are worth about .741, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and get their defensemen shooting (4th). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and their power play against the Devils’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Edmonton has scored 4.20 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Devils keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest) and keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). That means the Oilers’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much.

Connor McDavid (9 G / 30 A / 39 P in 15 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 16 A / 28 P in 15 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Arseny Gritsyuk (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Tristan Jarry (4-1-2 / .895 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to start for Edmonton, and Connor Hellebuyck (2-0-0 / .923 SV% in 2 GS) for New Jersey.
At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to send Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Formenton, Dickinson and Joseph.

Evan Bouchard has eight goals on chances worth about 3.1 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
